L178: ## Men's Lab Grown Diamond Rings
L179: 
L180: Draco Diamond stocks 22 men's lab grown diamond rings: eternity bands, Cuban link bands, weave bands and statement rings from 0.30ct to 15.05ct. White diamonds are IGI certified E to F colour, VS2 and better, with a few black and fancy colour designs named in the title. The collection opens at $947 CAD for a solid gold Cuban link band and $1,354 CAD for the first diamond set ring.
L181: 
L182: ## How do you choose a men's lab grown diamond ring?
L183: ### Width and comfort fit
L184: 
L185: Width changes fit at the same nominal size. A wide band contacts more of the finger and reads tighter, so wide designs often need a half size up. Comfort fit uses a domed interior that clears the knuckle and reduces flat contact. Measure warm, at the end of the day, on the finger you will actually wear it on.
L186: ### Metal durability
L187: 
L188: 10K gold is the hardest and most scratch resistant of the gold options. 18K is softer and richer in tone. Platinum is densest and holds detail for decades because scratches displace metal rather than remove it. Silver is softest and best for occasional wear. For a ring worn through manual work, 10K gold or platinum.
L189: ### Stone setting for daily wear
L190: 
L191: Setting matters more than carat on a ring that gets used. Channel and bezel hold stones at or below the metal line and absorb impact best: the 2.3ct dual channel band at $1,888 and the 5.4ct pear bezel dome ring at $3,299. Shared prong eternity bands, such as the 5ct oval at $2,599, release more light but expose more of each stone.
L192: ## What do men's lab grown diamond rings cost at Draco?
L193: Regular non sale prices run from $947 CAD to $4,488 CAD. Under $2,000: the plain solid gold Cuban link band at $947, the 0.30ct Cuban link ring at $1,354, the 2.55ct Crimson Thorns at $1,845 and the 2ct emerald half eternity at $1,899. Mid range covers the 4.9ct half eternity at $2,401 and the 5ct oval eternity at $2,599. Above $3,000 sit the 8ct eternity bands at $3,927 and $3,929, the 7.6ctw his and hers couple bands at $3,987 and the 15.05ct GOAT ring at $4,488.
L194: ## Certification and what ships with the ring
L195: 
L196: Multi stone pieces carry one IGI certificate for the piece. Single stone pieces carry a certificate per stone. Every order ships with its certificate. The report can be provided on request before purchase, and any IGI report can be verified free at IGI.org.
L197: Every Draco order includes: 30 day returns (customer pays return shipping, full refund, no restocking fee), Lifetime Authenticity Guarantee, free resizing, free insured worldwide shipping to 25 markets, signature on delivery, IGI certified E to F colour VS2 and better.
L198: 
L199: Frequently Asked
L200: ## Men's diamond ring questions
L201: 
L202: What size should I order for a wide band?
L203: 
L204: Go up a half size from your usual measurement. A wide band grips more of the finger and reads tighter at the same number. Resizing is included within 60 days of delivery, so order what you measure and adjust after wearing it.
L205: 
L206: Which metal holds up best for daily wear?
L207: 10K gold and platinum. 10K is the hardest gold option offered. Platinum is the densest and keeps its detail longest. 18K gold and silver suit lighter or occasional wear.
L208: 
L209: Can an eternity band be resized?
L210: 
L211: A full eternity band carries stones around the entire circumference, so size selection matters more than on other designs. A half eternity band, such as the 2ct emerald at $1,899, leaves plain metal at the back and adjusts more easily.
L212: 
L213: Will a lab grown diamond ring dull over time?
L214: The diamonds will not. They are Mohs 10 with no aging mechanism, so they do not cloud, fade or change colour. The metal is what shows wear. Inspect settings twice a year, more often on a ring worn constantly.
L215: 
L216: Are these the same as mined diamonds?
L217: 
L218: Chemically and optically, yes. A diamond tester measures thermal conductivity and a lab grown stone reads as diamond every time. Grading is done by the same laboratories against the same standards.

L313: Are lab grown diamonds real diamonds?
L314: 
L315: They are diamonds. A lab grown diamond is carbon crystal with the same physical and optical properties as a mined diamond, graded on the same scale by the same laboratories. It is Mohs 10 and has no aging mechanism, so it does not cloud or fade.

L318: Buy the largest well cut stone your budget allows within E to F colour and VS2 or better, then stop. Above VS2 the improvement is invisible without magnification and only the price moves.

L178: ## Men's Lab Grown Diamond Rings
L179: 
L180: Draco Diamond stocks 22 men's lab grown diamond rings: eternity bands, Cuban link bands, weave bands and statement rings from 0.30ct to 15.05ct. L181: 
L182: ## How do you choose a men's lab grown diamond ring?
L183: ### Width and comfort fit
L184: 
L185: Width changes fit at the same nominal size. A wide band contacts more of the finger and reads tighter, so wide designs often need a half size up. Comfort fit uses a domed interior that clears the knuckle and reduces flat contact. Measure warm, at the end of the day, on the finger you will actually wear it on.
L186: ### Metal durability
L187: 
L188: 10K gold is the hardest and most scratch resistant of the gold options. 18K is softer and richer in tone. Platinum is densest and holds detail for decades because scratches displace metal rather than remove it. Silver is softest and best for occasional wear. For a ring worn through manual work, 10K gold or platinum.
L189: ### Stone setting for daily wear
L190: 
L191: Setting matters more than carat on a ring that gets used. Channel and bezel hold stones at or below the metal line and absorb impact best: the 2.3ct dual channel band at $1,888 and the 5.4ct pear bezel dome ring at $3,299. Shared prong eternity bands, such as the 5ct oval at $2,599, release more light but expose more of each stone.
L192: ## What do men's lab grown diamond rings cost at Draco?
L193: Regular non sale prices run from $947 CAD to $4,488 CAD. Under $2,000: the plain solid gold Cuban link band at $947, the 0.30ct Cuban link ring at $1,354, the 2.55ct Crimson Thorns at $1,845 and the 2ct emerald half eternity at $1,899. Mid range covers the 4.9ct half eternity at $2,401 and the 5ct oval eternity at $2,599. L194: ## Certification and what ships with the ring
L195: 
L196: Multi stone pieces carry one IGI certificate for the piece. Single stone pieces carry a certificate per stone. Every order ships with its certificate. The report can be provided on request before purchase, and any IGI report can be verified free at IGI.org.
L197: Every Draco order includes: 30 day returns (customer pays return shipping, full refund, no restocking fee), Lifetime Authenticity Guarantee, free resizing, free insured worldwide shipping to 25 markets, signature on delivery, IGI certified E to F colour VS2 and better.
L198: 
L199: Frequently Asked
L200: ## Men's diamond ring questions
L201: 
L202: What size should I order for a wide band?
L203: 
L204: Go up a half size from your usual measurement. A wide band grips more of the finger and reads tighter at the same number. Resizing is included within 60 days of delivery, so order what you measure and adjust after wearing it.
L205: 
L206: Which metal holds up best for daily wear?
L207: 10K gold and platinum. 10K is the hardest gold option offered. Platinum is the densest and keeps its detail longest. 18K gold and silver suit lighter or occasional wear.
L208: 
L209: Can an eternity band be resized?
L210: 
L211: A full eternity band carries stones around the entire circumference, so size selection matters more than on other designs. A half eternity band, such as the 2ct emerald at $1,899, leaves plain metal at the back and adjusts more easily.
L212: 
L213: Will a lab grown diamond ring dull over time?
L214: The diamonds will not. They are Mohs 10 with no aging mechanism, so they do not cloud, fade or change colour. The metal is what shows wear. Inspect settings twice a year, more often on a ring worn constantly.
L215: 
L216: Are these the same as mined diamonds?
L217: 
L218: Chemically and optically, yes. A diamond tester measures thermal conductivity and a lab grown stone reads as diamond every time. Grading is done by the same laboratories against the same standards.
